subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI scroll fix be a renderer/viewport anchoring repair only, or should OpenClaw also add an explicit user-facing TUI auto-follow/scroll preference?
rationale: The source-backed problem is real enough to keep open, but choosing a dependency patch, local workaround, persisted setting, or in-session control changes TUI product behavior and possibly config surface.

options.title: Repair Anchoring First
options.body: Fix renderer/viewport stability as the default behavior, avoid new config unless proof shows users still need an explicit preference, and validate with PTY plus live terminal proof.

options.title: Add Opt-In Scroll Control
options.body: Add a TUI-owned auto-follow or jump-to-latest control if maintainers want visible user agency beyond the default stability fix.

options.title: Wait For Dependency Fix
options.body: Keep tracking upstream pi-tui and only bump/patch OpenClaw once the dependency owns the redraw behavior cleanly.

recommendation.title: Repair Anchoring First
recommendation.body: Fix renderer/viewport stability as the default behavior, avoid new config unless proof shows users still need an explicit preference, and validate with PTY plus live terminal proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available product-routing candidate from recent TUI runtime/docs history and dependency-surface context.
